description: God warned Isaiah not to think like everyone else, not to call everything a conspiracy, and not to live in dread. A word that feels written for right now.
excerpt: We are consuming so much of the same content, watching the same shows, scrolling the same feeds, following the same voices, that our thinking has quietly conformed to the world around us without us even noticing.
verse: The Lord has given me a strong warning not to think like everyone else does. He said, "Don't call everything a conspiracy, like they do, and don't live in dread of what frightens them."
body_html:
This verse feels like it was written for right now.

The Lord has given me a strong warning not to think like everyone else does.

That is where it starts. And that is exactly where a lot of us are missing it. We are consuming so much of the same content, watching the same shows, scrolling the same feeds, following the same voices, that our thinking has quietly conformed to the world around us without us even noticing.

God is calling us to something different. Not to be weird for the sake of being weird. But to think according to His truth and not according to the noise of everyone else.

Then He gets specific about what that looks like.

Don't call everything a conspiracy, like they do.

That one caught me because it fits our culture so well. Everything is a conspiracy right now. Every news story. Every event. Every headline. There is always a deeper theory. Always someone connecting dots. Always another layer people are convinced you are missing.

Some of those things are real. There is genuine deception in the world. There are lies being told. Discernment is important. But God is warning here against a mindset where everything is suspicious. Where every story is really about something else. Where we spend all our time trying to figure out the plot behind the plot.

That kind of thinking wears people down. It makes you paranoid. It steals your peace. It makes it hard to trust anyone. And most importantly, it distracts you from what God is actually doing.

And don't live in dread of what frightens them.

This is the other side of it. We are not supposed to live in the same fear the world lives in. The world is scared. Scared of the economy. Scared of the next election. Scared of the next disease. Scared of the next war. Scared of what is going to happen next.

We are not called to that.

We serve a God who is on the throne. Who is not surprised by any of it. Who has already written the ending. And He is asking us to walk through this world with a different kind of clarity. Not naive. Not disengaged. Just not dominated by fear the way everyone else is.

The verse right after this makes it clear where our fear should be directed instead.

Make the Lord of Heaven's Armies holy in your life. He is the one you should fear.

If we fear Him, we do not have to fear anything else. Not the conspiracies. Not the headlines. Not the economy. Not the future. He is the only one worth fearing, and the fear of Him is the beginning of wisdom.

I want to think differently than the world thinks. I want to see clearly without seeing conspiracies behind every corner. I want to live with awareness but not with dread. I want the fear of the Lord to be so central in my life that everything else finds its proper size.
question: What kind of thinking has quietly been shaping you lately, and is it lining up with how God is asking you to see the world?
